question.text: Per Chapter 9, which of the following statements about Cat I/II versus Cat III strategies is CORRECT?

answer.text: Cat I/II primarily invest in unlisted and high-growth companies (start-ups, SMEs, infrastructure, pre-IPO) via PE/VC/Debt/Infra strategies, whereas Cat III deploys complex trading/hedge strategies (long-short, arbitrage, multi-strategy) which are OUTSIDE the Cat I/II Manager (XIX-D) scope.
Cat I/II and Cat III are identical in investment universe.
Cat III is a sub-category of Cat I.
Cat I/II cannot invest in unlisted securities.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9's opening line: 'Category I AIFs and Category II AIFs are primarily investing in unlisted and high-growth companies.' The XIX-D exam tests Cat I/II Manager knowledge and strictly excludes Cat III hedge strategies as correct answers. Cat III is a separate category (covered in XIX-E) with listed-market and hedge-style strategies. The Trap: Option B collapses the category distinction. Option C inverts the hierarchy. Option D contradicts the unlisted-focus thesis. Cross-Exam Context: This IS the defining XIX-D vs XIX-E distinction. XIX-C (now superseded) covered the all-cat superset. XIX-A covers Cat I/II distributor; XIX-B covers Cat III distributor.
